recommendation: Build B's structure, with A's Write and C's bench. B makes the product legible: the subject list keeps many projects in hand, and the board shows one origin becoming several pieces, with decisions carried into each. Inside a piece, use A's single editorial margin and one header line, so writing feels like a document. Put C's resume card (the paragraph you were in, and what Claude or Codex did since) at the top of B's Studio home. Each direction's top-three fixes still apply.

directions.name: Document-led
directions.short: The piece is the screen; sections visit as sheets.
directions.idea: The piece you are writing fills the screen, opened at the sentence you left off. Notes, decisions and sources live in a margin beside the passage they concern; the other ten sections slide over the document as sheets and drop you back on the same line.
notes: Opening
The last piece, scrolled to the paragraph you left, with an inline "Left off here — next: tighten the ending" marker; the margin's first line says what changed while you were away.
Switching

Project name or ⌘K opens a finder with left-off lines; sibling tabs for pieces from one origin; a slim rail with the outline above the twelve sections. Write and Read are modes; the rest open as sheets.
Best at
Long writing and revision. The text is never more than one Esc away and "where I left off" is a place in the text.
Costs
Gather and Develop work lives in sheets, not a home of its own; a project with no piece has nothing to land on; thin overview; long margins at real volume; sheets hide the document.
To build

Write becomes the resting state with a stored position; the 12-step sidebar collapses into the rail; the inspector becomes a permanent three-tab margin with note-to-passage anchors; carousel strip; media reverse index.
directions.summary: A is the best writing room of the three: the margin, Your words, protected-phrase checks and Focus make Write feel like a good editor's desk, and "left off" is a place in the text rather than a status card. It pays for that everywhere else. Projects are one click away but never in view, the carousel is a tall strip you scroll through rather than a sequence you see whole, and intake or research days happen in a sheet over a dimmed document. The fixes keep the document as home and give the other work enough room.
critique: Where am I, what can I do
You land on your own sentence with a dismissible "Left off here" marker and one next step. Nothing to read first.
The finder works, but projects are hidden behind the title. With six active projects there is no list in view and no sign which one is waiting on you.
A place for my own words
"Your words" anchored to a selection, in serif with a sand edge, clearly authored by Adrian; Direction opens with "In your own words".
Inline marker in the text, "Since you left: Claude added 3 source notes" with Show them.
Material is drop, list and drag into topics; Source is speakers, timestamps and click-to-correct, with corrections flowing to Decisions.
Points marked Sure / Unsure / Disputed with evidence counts; one-point thread kept, AI reply honestly not connected.
The strongest Write of the three: margin notes and passages light each other both ways; Focus hides the margin.
All six slides exist on one page, but as a tall 4:5 strip. At 1440×900 about one and a half slides are visible, so the sequence is read by scrolling, not seen.
Every asset lists "Used in: Article ¶3 · Carousel slide 2" and the links jump there.
Arrange reorders the parts, Audience shows reader frames with no marks, Outputs says in one line what each of the three is for.
Sibling tabs "Article · Carousel · Listing — from Conversation with Mei Lin", each edited on its own.
Decisions tab with a live intact/changed check on protected phrases, corrections from Source, rejected angles struck through.
One thin top line, a slim rail and the margin. Sheets dim the document instead of adding columns.

compare.How you switch: Title / ⌘K finder; sibling tabs for pieces; rail with outline and twelve sections opening as sheets.

directions.name: Studio by subject
directions.short: Each subject is a board: origins → understanding → pieces.
directions.idea: Work is organised around subjects: one origin and everything that grew from it. A subject opens as a board read left to right, Origins → Understanding → Expressions, so one origin becoming several separately edited pieces is the first thing you see.
notes: Opening
Studio home: Pick up where you left off, Waiting on you, Since you left (Claude and Codex, with times), and a tile per subject with miniatures of its pieces.
Switching

A permanent subject list with search and filters (All, Active, Waiting on me, Touched by Claude) and a state line per subject; the twelve sections as a tab row inside a subject, with a piece picker on piece-level sections.
Best at
One origin, many outputs as the structure itself; carry-forward chips on the board and an "inherits" column beside every piece; juggling many projects.
Costs
Two levels of navigation; a one-off post still needs a subject; the board needs ~1240px; Library and Collections fold into each subject; a 13-item tab row.
To build

Sidebar becomes the subject list; steps move to a tab row; new Board and Studio home screens; inspector becomes the inherits column; per-subject state line, left-off record and a waiting-on-you query.
directions.summary: B gives the clearest picture of the product itself: a subject board makes Origins → Understanding → Pieces visible, carry-forward travels as chips into every piece, and the subject list with "Waiting on me" makes six projects easy to hold. The carousel and Media are the best of the three. It loses most on chrome: a breadcrumb, a 13-tab row, a piece picker and a toolbar stack above the text, the tab row runs out of room at 1280px, and anything without a subject has nowhere to go.
critique: Where am I, what can I do
Studio home leads with "Pick up where you left off" and a Resume button, then what is waiting on you.
The strongest: permanent list with search, Waiting-on-me and Touched-by-Claude filters, and a state line per subject.

Above the text sit a breadcrumb, a 13-tab row, a piece picker and a toolbar: four rows. The tab row fits at 1440, but at 1280 Share and Outputs run past the edge.

directions.name: Workbench by resuming
directions.short: Opens on where you left off; tools on a rack.
directions.idea: The opening screen answers two questions across every project: what was I doing, and what is the next useful move. The twelve sections are tools on a rack, not stations in an order; a right-hand column carries the project's understanding and your own thoughts into every tool.
notes: Opening
The bench: one card for the last piece with the paragraph you were in and "Since you were here" (actor-labelled), then Next moves across all projects, then every active project on one line.
Switching
One-line project switcher top left, ⌘K finder over projects and tools, a twelve-tool rack with honest counts, an "In:" strip when the scope is All.
Best at
Coming back after a gap, juggling six or more pieces, seeing agent work with its actor where it matters.
Costs
Suggests rather than guides; counts must be true or the bench lies; three columns are dense at 1280px; ranking of next moves is hand-ordered.
To build

Sidebar becomes rack with counts; new bench route needs last-edited position, a changes-since feed and a next-moves query; global scope; inspector becomes the understanding column; deep links into lines, slides and assets.
directions.summary: C is the strongest answer to "where was I" and "which project": the bench is inviting, specific and honest about who did what, and every next move lands on the exact line or slide. Its weakness is the right-hand understanding column. It is useful, but it is open on every tool, it competes with Write's own editorial margin, it splits Adrian's own words between two boxes, and under All projects it shows one project while the work shows another. Fix the column and C needs very little else.
critique: Where am I, what can I do
The bench leads with one card, one button (Continue at ¶4) and a short list of next moves. No manual needed.
One-line switcher, ⌘K finder, "Everything active" list with j/k, and the In: strip under All.
A place for my own words
Two boxes: "Your thoughts — Adrian" in the column and "What I want this to say — Adrian" in Direction. It is not clear they are the same record, or which one an agent reads.
Resume card quotes the paragraph; Current understanding heads the column.
Material is an intake list (bring in, open in Source, mark processed). Source is a timed transcript where you click a line to correct it. Keep/remove review is honestly stubbed.
Claims marked Refuted / Likely / Unsure / Disputed, evidence quoted, "Discuss this point" shown as not connected yet.
Margin, highlight-on-click and Focus all work, but with the rack, margin and understanding column open the manuscript is squeezed; two right-hand rails both carry notes.
All slides on one canvas, edit text in place, drag grips to reorder, Codex slide marked not accepted.
"Used in" appears on kept items lower down; the new-import cards you see first don't show it, so placement is hidden at the decision point.
Arrange composes, Audience says it is for looking not editing, Export lives in Outputs. Three distinct jobs.
Outputs shows the recording first, then article, carousel, caption and shared note, each with its own state and tool.
Decisions, protected phrases, corrections and rejected angles, each with where it applies; choosing an angle moves the other to Rejected.

The understanding column is a third persistent rail on every tool. Under All projects it names the project you were working in while the screen lists all of them; on phone the sheet stays open over the work.
